options: Double underscore = element, double dash = modifier
Naming alone doesn't prevent specificity issues
explanation: BEM uses double underscore (__) for sub-elements and double dash (--) for modifiers; creates flat specificity and prevents cascade.

question:
Why does OOCSS (Object-Oriented CSS) advocate reusable components?
```css
/* OOCSS: separate structure from skin */
.box { width: 200px; padding: 10px; } /* structure */
.box--highlight { background: yellow; } /* skin */
```
explanation: OOCSS separates layout/structure from presentation; reusable objects reduce code duplication.
SMACSS organizes CSS into 5 categories: Base, Layout, Module, State (is-), Theme; aids maintainability.

question:
How should utility classes and component classes coexist without conflicts?
```html
<!-- Tailwind utility + component -->\n<button class="btn bg-blue-500 hover:bg-blue-600">Button</button>
```
options: Use component as base, utilities as overrides
Utilities override components due to specificity
explanation: Utilities typically have lower specificity; they can override components or extend them, depending on CSS order.

question:
How do CSS naming conventions prevent style pollution across components?
```css
.component-name { } /* BEM: .component-name__element--modifier */
.c-name { } /* abbreviation */
._component { } /* underscore prefix */
```
explanation: Naming conventions (BEM, prefixes) reduce accidental overrides; scoped CSS (Modules, Shadow DOM) prevents them entirely.

options: Create separate classes for each state
Use is- or has- prefix convention
State classes mixed with component rules
explanation: Use is-/has- prefixes for state classes; separate from component definition for clarity and scalability.
Grid enables component-level 2D layouts; flexbox for simple linear layouts; choice affects component design.
Extend if element serves the same purpose (buttons with variants); create new if purpose differs (link that looks like button).

question:
How should CSS file organization scale with project size?
```
small: single style.css
medium: components/, layout/, utilities/
large: component-based (each component owns its CSS)
```
explanation: Large projects benefit from component-based CSS organization; small projects can use single file or type-based structure.

question:
How does cascading conflict resolution scale with codebase size, and what strategies prevent it?
```css
/* Problem: deep cascade hard to override */
.header .nav .item { } /* 0,0,3,1 */

/* Solution: flatter selectors */
.nav-item { } /* 0,0,1,0 */
```
options: Specificity creep causes override wars; keep selectors shallow
explanation: Deep cascades create specificity conflicts; keep selectors flat and use methodology (BEM, OOCSS) to prevent creep.
